title: a month is compared
line: two dates that both give a month are compared to the month: the 1900 census gives Charlotte's birth as April 1882, which agrees with the file's 12 Apr 1882 to the month and says the record gives only the month; a WikiTree profile of a John William Davidson born December 1876, which a name search for John Y Davidson reached, disagrees with the file's 24 April 1876 in the same year, where comparing the years alone agreed

steps.say: the 1900 Lukens household page, on the owner's word that it is Charlotte's

agree.some: birth date agrees (record April 1882, tree 12 Apr 1882: month only; the record gives only the month)

expect.why: the census gives the month and the year, the file the day: they agree to the month, and the finding says the record gives only the month, never only a year

steps.say: the WikiTree profile Davidson-349, a namesake born in England, matched for John Y Davidson

disagree.some: birth date disagrees (record DEC 1876, tree 24 April 1876: same year, different month)

expect.why: December 1876 and 24 April 1876 lie in one year but in two months: the dates disagree, where comparing the years alone agreed
